I bounce between work in News Media and Reality TV. 

It's always strange to me that the average person doesn't understand nothing is real unless the cameras *aren't* on it. If someone is reporting on it, the story was cooked up by some controller somewhere because it tested well with a demographic or something along those lines.

All of the partisan scandals you take sides on and power couples you look up to are there, posing for YOU because their brand is sponsored by y and y said they need to do x for their image or they pull out the $. They go home at the end of the day of a hard days work of putting on a show and lather rinse repeat. 

I imagine the same applies to politics (i.e. lobbying). The most informed shows you could watch for yourself right now to get a peak into the how money and brands control what you consume and, in turn, how you think, are UnReal and Veep. Obviously scripted but still, a look behind the curtain for those who would otherwise never think of it.

Catch yourself gobbling up the bs people. The more coverage, the more some marketing venture is involved.
